sources.title: Volker John, Numerical Methods for Convection-Dominated Problems, lecture notes, Chapter 5
sources.locator: Full 71-page PDF fetched; Chapter 5, printed pp. 54–62, especially Definitions 5.14, 5.17, 5.21, Lemma 5.20, Theorem 5.22 and its proof, Corollaries 5.23–5.24, Remark 5.25, and Theorem 5.26 with its complete proof were read; Example 5.16 and the boundary-layer example were inspected.

contents.name: §5.1 and Definition 5.14: residual-weighted streamline perturbation and cell residual
contents.reason: The local definition retains the complete strong residual, including the diffusion second derivative on smooth trial extensions; P1 cell residuals then simplify because their cellwise Laplacian is zero.

contents.name: Example 5.16: exact constant-coefficient one-dimensional coth parameter and fitted P1 scheme
contents.reason: This source gives the exact coth formula; the local lemma independently proves positivity and the parameter bounds used in stability and error estimates.

contents.name: Definitions 5.17 and 5.21: multidimensional stabilized norm and admissible streamline parameter
contents.reason: The local branch keeps the reaction-divergence lower bound and states its own explicit small-parameter condition rather than importing unrestricted multidimensional stability.

contents.name: Lemma 5.20 and Theorem 5.22 with coercivity proof: SUPG consistency and parameter-dependent coercivity
contents.reason: The local constant-coefficient P1 proof specializes the residual identity and proves coercivity from its own cellwise energy identity.

contents.name: Theorem 5.26 and complete proof: SUPG interpolation, orthogonality, and mesh-dependent error estimate
contents.reason: The local proof follows the interpolation and orthogonality route while retaining the extra smooth-extension diffusion-residual term required by the chosen residual form.

contents.name: Theorem 5.26 and complete proof: interpolation terms in the multidimensional stabilized norm
contents.reason: The local C2 P1 theorem proves each consistency, coercivity, solvability, and approximation term under its separately stated coefficient restrictions.

contents.name: Example 5.30: one-dimensional convection-dominated layer and mesh-resolution limitation
contents.reason: The local two-cell example computes exact nodal fitting and the limiting interior-cell error directly.

contents.name: Remark 5.25: restrictions and caveats for stabilization parameters
contents.reason: The local definition makes its parameter bound explicit and does not promote the one-dimensional exact parameter to general meshes.

contents.name: Chapter 5 treatments of higher-order methods, transient variants, and other parameter branches
contents.reason: These variants use hypotheses and trial spaces outside the assigned stationary P1 scope; the local pages make no transfer of their estimates.

sources.title: Thomas J. R. Hughes, Guglielmo Scovazzi, and Leopoldo P. Franca, Multiscale and Stabilized Methods, Encyclopedia of Computational Mechanics, ICES Report 04-18 (2004)

contents.name: §3.1: resolved/unresolved (coarse/fine) decomposition of the solution space
contents.reason: The local definition fixes a finite-dimensional direct sum and gives every block map its domain and codomain.

contents.name: §3.2.1: exact fine-scale response driven by the unresolved residual
contents.reason: The local block system writes the exact fine component as the inverse fine operator applied to its residual.

contents.name: §3.2.1: exact Schur elimination and the induced resolved equation
contents.reason: The local proof derives the exact and approximate Schur systems and bounds their difference in induced norms.

contents.name: §3.2.2: localized residual closure as an approximation to the fine Green operator
contents.reason: The local theorem measures the operator defect T-G and explicitly assumes approximate Schur invertibility.

contents.name: §3.2.2: exact fine-scale Green operators are generally nonlocal
contents.reason: The local definition and page prose retain this caveat and do not identify a local closure with exact elimination.

contents.name: §3.2.1: finite-dimensional coarse/fine split and closure-defect illustration
contents.reason: The B-page example verifies sharpness by an exact two-dimensional block calculation.

contents.name: Later application-specific VMS models and turbulence closures
contents.reason: Those conclusions require PDE-specific spaces, boundary conditions, Green operators, and approximation estimates beyond the assigned finite block theorem.
